0025 — Choose ESLint with typescript-eslint for lint, Biome for format

Status: accepted

Problem

Offing has strict TypeScript, a custom quality checker, and Stryker, but no repository linter or formatter. Style and many type-safety bugs stay review work. Epic #1987 needs one written choice before later tasks add a formatter (#2045), type-aware lint with a shrinking baseline (#2046), bans on any and unsafe casts (#2047), and floating-promise / empty-catch rules (#2048).

On 2026-11-03, main still has none of ESLint, Biome, or Prettier in package.json. The gap is real; this record picks the tools only.

Options compared

Candidates named in the issue: ESLint with typescript-eslint, and Biome. Prettier is included only as the usual formatter pair for ESLint, so format speed has a measured baseline.

Axis ESLint + typescript-eslint Biome
Type-aware rules Uses the TypeScript program (projectService). typescript-eslint ships 63 rules that require type information, including no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, and the no-unsafe-* family. Own type inference (no tsc). Typed rules live under the types domain; noFloatingPromises is still nursery. Biome's own release notes put floating-promise recall at about 75% of typescript-eslint.
Formatter None built in; needs Prettier or Biome format. Built in; one binary for lint and format.
Upkeep Flat config + plugin surface; rule and version churn across ESLint and typescript-eslint. One package and one config; smaller ecosystem and fewer typed rules today.

Measurements

Same machine (Apple A18 Pro, Node.js v26.12.0), same tree tip, 479 hand-written .ts files under src/ and tools/ (vendor trees excluded). Tools were installed outside the repository so this record does not change dependencies. Versions: ESLint 10.14.0, typescript-eslint 8.72.1, Biome 2.6.4, Prettier 3.6.2, TypeScript 5.9.3. Wall-clock times are the median of three runs unless noted.

Run Config Median wall time Notes
tsc --noEmit repository tsconfig.json 57.7 s (one run) Full program check; reference for typed cost.
ESLint type-aware recommendedTypeChecked plus floating-promise / no-unsafe-* / no-explicit-any 16.9 s Exit 1; 152 problems on this corpus (unsafe assignments/members/args, unnecessary assertions, await-thenable, and related).
Biome lint recommended + noExplicitAny 0.61 s Exit 1; 69 errors, 809 warnings (many noNonNullAssertion).
Biome lint (typed) domains.types + domains.project = all, plus nursery noFloatingPromises 0.88 s Exit 1; 135 errors. Extra cost is small; findings were mostly noUndeclaredDependencies and noImplicitAnyLet, not floating promises.
Biome format check biome ci --linter-enabled=false 0.81 s Exit 1; 369 files would change under the trial config.
Prettier --check same 479 files 27.8 s Exit 1; 407 files would change.

On a small fixture both tools catch a naked returnsPromise() call and an as any cast. On this repository, ESLint's program-backed no-unsafe-* rules fire in volume; Biome has no equivalent family backed by tsc, and noFloatingPromises reported no hits here while still marked nursery.

Decision

  1. Lint with ESLint and typescript-eslint, with type-aware rules enabled through the TypeScript project service. Later epic tasks turn on the typed rules they need and keep baselines that can only shrink.
  2. Format with Biome (formatter only for the default check path). Biome's format check is about 30× faster than Prettier on this corpus and keeps formatting in one Rust binary without a third JS toolchain.
  3. Do not use Biome as the type-aware linter for the #1987 exit criteria. Approximate inference and nursery typed rules are not enough for "forbid floating promises with no baseline left" and for unsafe-cast coverage that matches the TypeScript checker already in the repo.
  4. Do not add Prettier. Format belongs to Biome; lint belongs to ESLint. Disable Biome's linter (or leave it unused) in the default npm run check path so the two tools do not fight over the same diagnostics.

This record chooses the tools only. Installing them, formatting the tree, and wiring rules into npm run check are later issues in the epic.

Why

  • Typed lint is the scarce resource. Follow-ups need rules that read the real TypeScript program. That is typescript-eslint's job today; Biome's inference is faster but incomplete by its own numbers.
  • Format is a speed and upkeep problem. Once lint is settled on ESLint, Biome format beats Prettier on measured wall time here and avoids maintaining Prettier alongside ESLint.
  • One responsibility each. Splitting lint and format keeps typed-rule upgrades in the ESLint config and format policy in biome.json, which matches how #2045 and #2046 are split.

Consequences

  • #2045 adds Biome 2.6.4 as a devDependency, wires format:check into npm run check, and formats the tree in one commit; unformatted code fails the check. Re-wrapping src/sdk.ts and src/mcp.ts in that commit changes whitespace only, so neither public contract changes.
  • #2046 adds ESLint with typescript-eslint, enables type-aware rules, and records a shrinking baseline.
  • #2047 and #2048 tighten typed rules on top of that ESLint config.
  • No runtime dependency and no network use in scans. DevDependency pins and exact rule sets land in the implementation pull requests, not here.
